claims.text: An active-learning neural-network-potential workflow can accurately predict fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The proposed workflow can retain vibrational-entropy contributions to phase free energies.
The proposed workflow can retain anharmonic contributions to phase free energies.
The proposed neural-network potential can retain electron–vibration coupling.
The workflow will be substantially less expensive than explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics free-energy calculations.
The workflow will significantly outperform TOR-TILD for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Active learning on a sparse set of ab initio molecular-dynamics trajectories can replace exhaustive explicit ab initio sampling.
A trained neural-network potential can be used to compute free energies for both solid and liquid phases.
The method is extendable from elemental and binary systems to multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Interatomic-potential simulations can be applied to a five-component high-entropy alloy and reproduce some first-principles and experimental properties.
The neural-network potential captures subtle electronic and vibrational effects with minimal ab initio input.
Interpolation between selected ab initio configurations and active sampling of outliers efficiently reproduce the relevant free-energy landscape.
The surrogate reduces the number of costly molecular-dynamics steps without losing the physics needed for phase-transition predictions.
Free-energy predictions will differ from full ab initio molecular dynamics by approximately 5–10%.
Computational cost will be reduced by approximately one to two orders of magnitude relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The methodology is valid for alloys containing up to about five elements.
The methodology is valid across solid, near-melting, and liquid temperatures.
